newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: KERNOT SAYS WALLIS REPORT A MIXED BAG
Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot has accused the Wallis Inquiry into Australia's financial system of "whimping out" on the issue of bank fees and charges.
Senator Kernot has criticised the report for not putting a ceiling on bank fees and charges, and says it basically means that banks can charge what they like.
But speaking at a National Consumers Federation conference in Melbourne, Senator Kernot praised the report for saying "on record" that foreign bank ownership is not in Australia's national interest.
QLD WILL FOLLOW CONSTITUTION IF COLSTON GOES, SAYS PREMIER
The Queensland Premier, Rob Borbidge, says if Senator Mal Colston resigns the Queensland Parliament will respect its constitutional obligations.
In the past Premier Rob Borbidge has said he'd appoint an independent if Senator Colston was forced to resign over irregularities in his travel claims.
But Mr Borbidge says since the Senator will remain in the Senate until he's ineligible or resigns, it's not a Queensland problem.
KOSCIUSKO BECOMES KOSCIUSZKO
It's official...the name of Australia's highest peak is to be spelt differently.
But, we'll still say Kosciusko.
The state government has ruled that the missing "z" should be restored to the spelling of Kosciusko, but it's decided that the pronunciation won't change.

Land and Conservation Minister, Kim Yeadon said he's accepted the recommendation of the Geographical Names Board to add a "z" to the spelling of the mountain, but he says that aside from being a typists' nightmare, adding an accent would not be something he believed most Australians would want.

The Minister says the change in spelling will be a fitting way to acknowledge the achievements of the explorer, Paul Edmund Strzelecki, who named Mount Kosciusko after the 18th century Polish patriot, Kosciuszko (pron: Kos-shu--xko).
Mr Yeadon says the cost of the change should be minimal because signs and maps can be altered as they're repaired or re-printed.
NSW CONFIDENT OF ALLAYING ANTHRAX FEARS
The New South Wales Department of Agriculture is confident Australia's safety measures will quell Indonesia's fears about anthrax in Australian beef.
An Indonesian delegation to Sydney today comes after Indonesia extended its ban on all New South Wales beef and live cattle exports until the end of April, following isolated outbreaks of anthrax.
Indonesia is concerned the disease could be passed from contaminated beef to humans.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
